what_it_is.prose: The Pinaka Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher is India's indigenous artillery rocket system, designed by DRDO's ARDE Pune, RCI Hyderabad, and DRDL Hyderabad laboratories. The system is produced by a consortium of TASL and L&T (launchers), Economic Explosives Limited (EEL/Solar Group) and Munitions India Limited (MIL) for rockets, and BEML for vehicles. The Pinaka family spans eight variants: Mk-I (37.5 km range), Mk-I Enhanced / Enhanced Pinaka Rocket System (EPRS, 45 km), Mk-II (60 km), Guided Pinaka (75 km), Mk-II ER (90 km), LRGR-120 / Mk-III (120 km), Mk-IV (300 km planned), and ELRGR (300+ km). Each launcher fires 12 rockets in a 44-second salvo. The LRGR-120 rocket weighs 535 kg with a 110 kg warhead, is 4.8 m long, has a 300 mm calibre, achieves Mach 4.7 max speed, reaches 40 km flight altitude, and has a Circular Error Probable (CEP) of less than 30 metres. Unit cost is approximately ₹2.3 crore per system (~$240k) and ₹430 crore per regiment (~$53M). Seven Pinaka regiments are operational as of March 2026 (the 7th regiment was inducted in March 2026, the 4th was raised, and the last 2 are expected in 2027), with a target of 10 by mid-2026 and 22 long-term. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared the LRGR-120 programme on 29 December 2025 for ₹2,500 crore (~$260M). On 6 February 2025, a ₹10,147 crore (~$1.1B) ammunition contract was signed — EEL received ₹4,500 crore for Area Denial Munition (ADM) and MIL received ₹5,647 crore for High Explosive Pre-Fragmented (HEPF) Mk-1(E) rockets. Pinaka was first used in combat during the Kargil War in 1999 (in its Mk-I form), and has since been exported in discussion to Armenia.

faq.question: What is the LRGR-120 variant of Pinaka?
faq.answer: LRGR-120 (Long Range Guided Rocket, 120 km) is the Mk-III variant of the Pinaka family. The rocket weighs 535 kg with a 110 kg warhead, is 4.8 m long, has a 300 mm calibre, achieves Mach 4.7 max speed, reaches 40 km flight altitude, and has a Circular Error Probable (CEP) of less than 30 metres. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared the LRGR-120 programme on 29 December 2025 for ₹2,500 crore (~$260M). Pre-production units are being manufactured by Economic Explosives Limited (EEL).

faq.question: How many Pinaka regiments does the Indian Army operate?
faq.answer: Seven Pinaka regiments were operational as of March 2026 (the 7th regiment was inducted in March 2026, the 4th was raised, and the last 2 are expected in 2027). The target is 10 regiments by mid-2026 and 22 long-term. Each regiment comprises approximately 12 launchers, command posts, and support vehicles.

faq.question: Has Pinaka been exported?
faq.answer: Armenia has been reported as an export customer for the Pinaka MBRL system, marking the first export of an Indian artillery rocket system. The exact contract value and delivery timeline have not been officially confirmed by the Indian MoD or the production consortium (TASL + L&T + EEL + MIL + BEML). Pinaka's successful combat debut in the 1999 Kargil War and its continued evolution through eight variants (Mk-I 37.5 km to planned Mk-IV 300 km) position it well for further exports to friendly foreign countries.
